t: Hill chiefs of the Malnad who rose as Western Chalukya feudatories and became an independent kingdom under Veera Ballala II in 1187.
Their soapstone temples at Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura, on star-shaped platforms, are World Heritage masterpieces of sculpture.
Weakened by the Delhi Sultanate’s invasions from 1311, the dynasty ended when Veera Ballala III was killed in 1343.
dyk: Many Hoysala temple sculptures are signed: carvers such as Mallitamma and Dasoja left their names beside their work, unusually for medieval India.
ev: Vishnuvardhana’s forces take Talakad from the Cholas
The Chennakeshava temple at Belur is consecrated
Veera Ballala II assumes full imperial titles
Ballala II defeats the Seuna Yadavas at Soratur
The Keshava temple at Somanathapura is built
Malik Kafur captures the Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra
Veera Ballala III is killed fighting the Madurai Sultanate

f.capital: Sosevur; Belur; then Dwarasamudra (Halebidu); later Tiruvannamalai
f.founder: Sala (legendary); Nripa Kama II (earliest attested chief)
